data.name: Octavina
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Roman numeral octo (eight) and the Latin word 'vina' (wine), Octavina refers to a 'wealthy eight' or 'wealthy vine'. This name has Latin and Roman origins and has been used in Christian tradition, particularly in reference to Saint Octavian of Siena.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes abundance and prosperity in spiritual and material aspects of life.

in_hebrew.name: אוקטבינה
in_hebrew.meaning: בת העשרה, שמחה, חגיגה, חג שדרות, יום חג, חג
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אוקטבינה: שם נשים שמקורו באוקטב, שפירושו 8, ואינה, שפירושו 1. בעברית, 8 ציינה את כניסת ישראל לארץ ישראל. אוקטבינה היא שם נשים שסגנונו על-ספרדי, והוא נפוץ בעיקר בקרב יהודים-קראים. השם עשוי ללקות בטעות, ועלול להפוך לאוקטביה, שהיא שם נשים שמקורו באוקטב, כאמור, ובאינה. אבל, בעולם הנוצרי, אוקטבינה נמנה עם שמות הקדושים, וזהו שם שמועותיו.

in_greek.name: Οκταβίνα
in_greek.meaning: παιδί των οκτώ, χαρά, εορτή, εορτασμός, ημέρα εορτής, εορτή
in_greek.long_meaning: Οκταβίνα: γυναικείο όνομα που προέρχεται από τον όρο Οκτάβος, που σημαίνει 8 και η Ινα, που σημαίνει 1. Στη Βυζαντινή Αυτοκρατορία, η Οκταβίνα ήταν ένα κοινό όνομα για τα κορίτσια. Ο Οκταβιανός, γιος του Αυγούστας, ήταν ο επόμενος Αυτοκράτορας της Ρώμης και ο πρώτος με το όνομα Αυτοκράτορας. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ο Οκταβιανός είναι ο πρώτος Αυτοκράτορας της Ρώμης που αναφέρεται ως Αύγουστος.

in_latin.name: Octavina
in_latin.meaning: filia octava, gaudeo, festus, celebratio, dies festus, festa
in_latin.long_meaning: Octavina: nomen femininum quod a Octavo, qui significat 8, et a Io, qui significat 1, derivatur. In ecclesia catholica, Octavina est nomen quod significat Octavam Diei Dominici, qua dies festus est. In antiquo, Octaviana erat nomen quod dabant matres ad infantia sua.

data.cultural_impact: In the Roman Catholic tradition, Saint Octavian, whose given name was Girolamo, is recognized as a miraculous healer and extraordinary preacher. He was born on October 8, 1575, and he is often depicted in art with a wine glass or a vine in his hand, symbolizing his spiritual connection to the sacrament of the Eucharist and his devoted service to the Church. Therefore, the name Octavina, which means 'wealthy vine', can be seen as a nod to this saint's connection to both spiritual wealth and the Christian sacrament of the Eucharist.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Octavina carries deep spiritual meaning as it reminds us of the richness and abundance that come from our faith. Not only does it evoke the image of a lush vine, yielding an abundant harvest, but it also echoes the blessings we receive in our spiritual journey. In the Christian tradition, the vine and its branches symbolize Christ and the Church, whom we are connected through faith. This name serves as a reminder to those who bear it that they too are integral parts of the spiritual vine, and that like the branches, they too produce fruit in His name.

historical_references.reference: Octavina was a form of the name Octavia, which was popular among the ancient Roman nobility. The name is derived from the Latin word 'octo' meaning 'eight' and 'viam' meaning 'road'. Octavian, who later became Augustus Caesar, had a sister named Octavia whom he held in high esteem. He adopted her young niece, Octavia Minor, who became his second wife. Octavia Minor's name was later latinized to Octavina and became a popular Christian name in the early centuries AD.
historical_references.time_period: Early Roman Republic to Early Christian Era (6th century BC to 4th century AD)

historical_references.reference: During the Middle Ages, Octavina was the name of several saints, including St. Octavina of Piacenza, a martyr who lived in the 4th century AD. According to legend, she was a servant girl who was tortured and killed for refusing to renounce her Christian faith. Her memory was revered by the local Christian community and she was later canonized.
